newsitem.title: FRANCE: MAS's 777 arrival on Paris-Kuala lifts cargo capac.
newsitem.headline: MAS's 777 arrival on Paris-Kuala lifts cargo capac.

text.p: Malaysian Air System said cargo capacity on its three-times weekly Paris/Charles de Gaulle-Kuala Lumpur passenger route had probably increased slightly with the introduction of Boeing 777s earlier this month.

"We are just beginning to familiarise ourselves with the 777 and its cargo-carrying capabilities so it's difficult to draw comparisons with the 747s we operated on the route previously but it's likely it offers a little more capacity. Certainly, it is a very practical aircraft for palletised freight," a Paris-based MAS cargo official told Reuters.

"Our Vienna cargo station has loaded up to 24 tonnes of freight on to a 777 bound for Kuala Lumpur with a full passenger compliment and favourable weather conditions so we have a rough idea of what capacity we have available from Paris," the official added.
Two of the three 777 frequencies are non-stop from Paris whilst the third which currently makes a stopover at Munich, will be non-stop from July 10.
Effective June 1, MAS has a 30-tonne allocation on one of Air France' Boeing 747-200F two weekly flights on the route.

MAS' Paris cargo station also has cargo space allocations on the airline's freighter services from Amsterdam and Frankfurt to Kuala Lumpur, the official added. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
